P-aur00001.text: Bajra (Pearl Millet) - Crop Water Requirement: 300-400 mm. Bajra is the most drought-tolerant cereal crop suitable for semi-arid regions. It can produce reasonable yields even with 250-300 mm of well-distributed rainfall. Recommended varieties for Marathwada: ICTP 8203, Dhanashakti, AHB 1200. Optimal sowing: onset of monsoon, June 15 - July 15.
P-aur00001.doc_title: Crop-Water Requirements for Maharashtra Dryland Agriculture
P-aur00001.publishing_body: ICAR - Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture
P-aur00001.section: Millets - Water Requirements and Drought Tolerance

P-aur00002.text: Tur (Pigeon Pea / Arhar) - Crop Water Requirement: 600-650 mm. Tur is a deep-rooted, drought-tolerant legume with biological nitrogen fixation ability. Duration: 160-180 days for medium varieties. In deficit rainfall years, tur's deep root system (up to 2m) helps access subsoil moisture. Sowing window: June first fortnight. Recommended spacing for rainfed conditions: 90 cm × 20 cm.
P-aur00002.doc_title: Kharif Crop Advisory for Marathwada Region

P-aur00003.text: Mung Bean (Green Gram) - Crop Water Requirement: 300-350 mm. Short duration crop (60-75 days). Highly suitable as a catch crop in seasons with uncertain rainfall. Drought escape strategy due to short duration. Improves soil fertility through nitrogen fixation (20-25 kg N/ha). Suitable varieties: Virat, BM-4, IPM 02-3.
P-aur00003.doc_title: Short Duration Crops for Climate Resilience in Dryland Farming
P-aur00003.publishing_body: ICAR - Indian Institute of Pulses Research

P-aur00004.text: Protective Irrigation in Dryland Agriculture: In deficit rainfall seasons, one or two protective irrigations at critical crop growth stages can increase yields by 30-50%. Critical stages for millets: boot/heading stage and grain filling. Water requirement for protective irrigation: 40-50 mm per irrigation. Mulching with crop residues reduces evaporation by 20-30% and maintains soil moisture.
P-aur00004.doc_title: Water Management in Dryland Farming Systems

P-aur00005.text: Cotton should be avoided in seasons where rainfall is projected below 600mm as the crop requires 700-1300mm water and is highly sensitive to moisture stress during square formation and boll development. Similarly, Soybean requires well-distributed rainfall of 600-800mm; yield reduction is severe (40-60%) when rainfall drops below 450mm during pod filling stage.
P-aur00005.doc_title: Seasonal Crop Planning Advisory - Aurangabad Division
P-aur00005.section: Crops to Avoid in Deficit Rainfall Years

P-tnj00002.text: Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) in Rice: AWD technique saves 15-25% irrigation water compared to continuous flooding without significant yield reduction. The field is allowed to dry until hairline cracks appear before re-irrigation. This technique also reduces methane emissions by 30-40%. Suitable for areas with reliable water access but conservation goals.
P-tnj00002.doc_title: Water Saving Technologies in Rice Cultivation
